overall: Bounded source/assertion review of §7.11 and §14.13. Public external-file consumers traced prefer UF. New nested Form/Type3/pattern MCAF controls are parent-integrated; see parent-review for execution and corrected draft premises. All carriers/keys are not certified.

features.source_location: ISO md §7.11.1–.2.2 lines 3854–3903; primary printed pp. 131–133 (physical pp. 146–148). §7.11.2.1 explicitly says components are bytes; §7.11.2.2 gives two path-resolution examples and URL-relative restrictions.
features.errata: No applicable EC3 change found in this sampled clause set.
features.ledger: 7.11.1, 7.11.2, 7.11.2.1, 7.11.2.2 (implemented). Their notes claim both forms, escaping/empty components, byte preservation, two relative-resolution examples, and URL component restrictions.
features.code: crates/pdf-model/src/file_spec.rs: FileSpec::parse, components, is_absolute, resolve_against, is_valid_relative_url.
features.tests: crates/pdf-model/tests/file_specifications_audit.rs (valid xref/no-recovery, both forms, byte/path behavior and defaults); unit tests in file_spec.rs cover clause examples.
features.assertions: The integration test asserts indirect simple string resolution, escaped/display dictionary name, V/ID, default values, and a legacy Unix entry. Unit tests assert RFC3986 restrictions and the two relative examples. These establish those sampled outputs, not host filesystem behavior; this tree intentionally does not open a path. Existing FileSpec unit test deliberately asserts a split contract: display_name returns the Unicode /UF spelling while components still returns raw /F bytes. The standalone candidate makes relative-vs-absolute /F-vs-/UF behavior explicit and also captures the disputed URL case; it documents current API scope and does not encode a normative failure.
features.verdict: implemented with a possible consumer-facing representation inconsistency
features.residuals: components(), is_absolute(), and resolve_against() read FileSpec.bytes, which from_dictionary fills from /F before considering /UF. Table 43 says a PDF reader shall use /UF when present instead of /F. display_name correctly prefers /UF, but there is no caller of components() outside tests found in this scan, so immediate public behavior impact is unestablished. URL accessor also reads /F; §7.11.5 specifically defines the URL in /F while Table 43 has general /UF precedence. Test the conflict for ordinary filesystem paths first; do not assert network behavior. Follow-up trace: all observed filesystem-opening consumers receive a String chosen with FileSpec::display_name (UF first): Table 203 GoToR and Table 204 GoToE use action::target_root; Table 253 FDF named-page Reference::read explicitly chooses UF then F; §12.7.6.4 ImportData uses FileSpec::display_name; viewer-host::policy::resolve_import only splits that caller-provided string and applies sandbox path rules. No production consumer calls FileSpec::components/is_absolute/resolve_against, which are currently standalone model helpers. Existing unit test `the_unicode_name_is_used_instead_of_the_byte_string` deliberately asserts components use raw F bytes; that is an explicit API contract but it conflicts with interpreting those methods as the reader-effective path. A scratch discriminator is in drafts/file_spec_path_precedence_candidate.rs. SubmitForm and deprecated media URL cases use FileSpec::url(), which reads F specifically; URL conflict remains an ambiguity between Table 43 general UF precedence and §7.11.5 F-as-URL.

features.verdict: Sampled display-name preference is correct; raw helper API is not proof of effective reader path selection.
features.residuals: The current integration test's distinct /F and /UF establishes display_name only. from_dictionary stores /F in bytes even when /UF exists, and path helpers consume bytes. The source says /UF instead of /F for a reader, so either select /UF for operations (with a documented byte-preservation policy) or narrow these helpers to raw legacy bytes and ensure no reader consumer treats them as preferred resolved path. The local model currently shows no non-test caller to components()/resolve_against(), so rate as an unproven feature-contract mismatch until public consumer evidence is found. Table 43 writer requirements (Type/EF/EP/RF indirection, required F, wrapper filename privacy) do not imply parser rejection obligations.

features.assertions: The EC3 example audit exercises catalog embedding, marked-content MCAF array route, direct array-valued property resource, and an XObject. Page/external/annotation tests separately assert names, relationships, and embedded payload availability. The source specifies carrier shape and relationship; it does not require rejecting malformed producers. External-associated files are listed by name and relationship while their bytes are not fetched. New scratch-only candidate nested_marked_content_associated_files.rs provides three exact-xref/no-recovery public Interpretation tests: AF-tagged MCAF inside a Form XObject, inside a Type 3 CharProc, and inside a tiling pattern cell. Each uses a distinct target filename, literal /Desc, /AFRelationship and embedded stream with the §14.13.2 ModDate, plus an ordinary /Span with a decoy MCAF and ordinary text control. Ranges assert the exact nested text or empty text range for painted pattern geometry. Not run by this auditor.
features.verdict: strongly implemented across sampled carrier routes; bounded audit does not certify all carriers and UI exposure
features.residuals: Caller trace resolves nested content: page dictionary AF is exposed by viewer-core attachment answers; catalog AF and EmbeddedFiles are enumerated by attachment::attachments; annotations direct AF is collected by pointer::attached_files and the panel. Structure elements and DParts have explicit traversal; XObject direct AF is supported through associated() and an XObject attachment test. MCAF is processed by run::marked_ops and returned on the public page Interpretation; Type 3, Forms, and tiling patterns recurse through the same Interpreter::run. New scratch candidate gives direct public-report assertions for Form/Type3/tiling. Annotation appearance MCAF has no content-interpretation report route; metadata-stream AF has no public attachment enumeration callsite. These are implementation/API exposure boundaries, not missing mandated panel behavior: §14.13.1 does not require a processor to list every association, and ADR 2799 intentionally scopes external-file panel population to catalog and page-in-view. The broad `associated()` model parser can parse any dictionary, but that does not mean those other carriers reach a consumer. The ledger should state this exact boundary rather than imply full public enumeration.
